'''Scott Hocknull''' (born 1977) is an Australian [[palaeontologist]] specialising in fossil vertebrates and Senior Curator in [[Geology]] at the [[Queensland Museum]] in [[Brisbane]]. He was the 2002 recipient of the [[List of Young Australian of the Year Award recipients|Young Australian of the Year Award]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Young Australian of the Year 2002|url=http://www.australianoftheyear.org.au/honour-roll/?view=fullView&year=2002&recipientID=145|publisher=[[National Australia Day Council]]|accessdate=29 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202103614/http://www.australianoftheyear.org.au/honour-roll/?view=fullView&year=2002&recipientID=145|archive-date=2 February 2014}}</ref>

He is the youngest Australian to date to hold a museum curatorship and has described and named 10 new species and four new genera,<ref>[http://www.unsw.edu.au/news/pad/articles/2002/jan/studentYoungAust.html Profile at UNSW.edu]</ref> including (in cooperation with the original finder Robyn Mackenzie) a giant [[Sauropod]] ''[[Australotitan]] cooperensis''.<ref name="PeerJ">[https://peerj.com/articles/11317/ Hocknull SA, Wilkinson M, Lawrence RA, Konstantinov V, Mackenzie S, Mackenzie R. 2021. A new giant sauropod, ''Australotitan cooperensis gen. et sp. nov.'', from the mid-Cretaceous of Australia. PeerJ 9:e11317], persistent access [https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.11317 doi]</ref>

== Awards ==
* National and Queensland Career Achiever, 2002
* Queensland Science and Technology Achiever, 2002
* National Career Achiever, 2002
* Centenary Medalist, 2003
* Neville Stephens Medal, [[Geological Society of Australia]], 2005
* Riversleigh Medal, 2009
* Rising Stars of Queensland Science, 2015
* 10 Best of the Best of Queensland's 50 Top Thinkers, 2015
